name: Arkady and a Nobody-men
description: Arkady words in a large company. There are n employees working in a system of a strict hierarchy. Namely, each employee, with an exception of the CEO, has exactly one immediate manager. The CEO is a manager (through a chain of immediate managers) of all employees. Each employee has an integer rank. The CEO has rank equal to 1 , each other employee has rank equal to the rank of his immediate manager plus 1 . Arkady has a good post in the company, however, he feels that he is nobody in the company's structure, and there are a lot of people who can replace him. He introduced the value of replaceability . Consider an employee a and an employee b , the latter being manager of a (not necessarily immediate). Then the replaceability r ( a , b ) of a with respect to b is the number of subordinates (not necessarily immediate) of the manager b , whose rank is not greater than the rank of a . Apart from replaceability, Arkady introduced the value of negligibility . The negligibility z a of employee a equals the sum of his replaceabilities with respect to all his managers, i.e. , where the sum is taken over all his managers b . Arkady is interested not only in negligibility of himself, but also in negligibility of all employees in the company. Find the negligibility of each employee for Arkady.
input_specification: The first line contains single integer n ( 1 ≤ n ≤ 5·10 5 ) — the number of employees in the company. The second line contains n integers p 1 , p 2 , ..., p n ( 0 ≤ p i ≤ n ), where p i = 0 if the i -th employee is the CEO, otherwise p i equals the id of the immediate manager of the employee with id i . The employees are numbered from 1 to n . It is guaranteed that there is exactly one 0 among these values, and also that the CEO is a manager (not necessarily immediate) for all the other employees.
output_specification: Print n integers — the negligibilities of all employees in the order of their ids: z 1 , z 2 , ..., z n .
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 860E — Arkady and a Nobody-men [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
